Spinner I has outcomes: \(2,3,4,5\)  
Spinner II has outcomes: \(1,3,5,7,9\)

There are \(4 \times 5 = 20\) equally likely products.

Check each outcome from Spinner I:

- If Spinner I is \(2\): products are  
  \(2,6,10,14,18\)  
  Two-digit even products: \(10,14,18\), so \(3\) outcomes.

- If Spinner I is \(3\): products are  
  \(3,9,15,21,27\)  
  None are even.

- If Spinner I is \(4\): products are  
  \(4,12,20,28,36\)  
  Two-digit even products: \(12,20,28,36\), so \(4\) outcomes.

- If Spinner I is \(5\): products are  
  \(5,15,25,35,45\)  
  None are even.

Total favorable outcomes: \(3+4=7\)

Thus, the probability is  
\[
\frac{7}{20}
\]

The answer is \(\frac{7}{20}\).
